reason: The cited evidence does not address the key premises. E1 reports strength and ductility in a dual-phase TiZrMoW HEA without mentioning coherent nanoprecipitates or SCCPs. E2 discusses interstitial elements (C, N, O) in NiCoCr, not coherent precipitates. E3 describes deformation mechanisms (dislocation slip, twinning) in Al0.3CoCrFeNi, with no reference to precipitates. None of the cited passages provide specific prior evidence for the formation, role, or high-temperature behavior of coherent nanoprecipitates as hypothesized.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can be formed in refractory HEAs via stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs).
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion, increasing strength.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer, delaying plastic instability and enhancing toughness.
The proposed mechanism operates at high temperatures (600–800 °C) in refractory alloys for plasma-facing components.
